difficulty.from: question type (detail); the RC bank has no difficulty field

answer.text: folds its membrane inward around every fungal branch
answer.line: Paragraph 3 says the plant cell does not simply give way: its own membrane stretches inward around every branch.

steps: Find the arbuscule: paragraph 3, sentences 2 to 5.
Read what the plant cell does. The cell does not give way; its membrane stretches inward around every branch.
That keeps two membranes between them. The fungus gets inside the wall, never into the cytoplasm.

choices.text: dissolves its own wall so the two organisms can mix freely
choices.note: The fungus breaches the wall, but sentence 5 says the two never share cytoplasm. Nothing mixes freely.

choices.text: wraps the fungus in a dense sheath of its own tissue
choices.note: A dense sheath is the mantle from paragraph 4: fungal tissue around a root tip, not plant tissue around the fungus.

choices.text: folds its membrane inward around every fungal branch
choices.note: Sentence 5: its own membrane stretches inward around every branch.

choices.text: fills with stored lipid that the fungus later draws on
choices.note: Lipid is stored in vesicles, sentence 6, which are swollen fungal hyphae. The plant cell is not the store.

choices.text: dies off, leaving a cavity that the fungus then occupies
choices.note: Sentence 4 says the plant cell does not simply give way. A dead cell could not stretch its membrane around the branches.
